description: Schematic clip zones used to build approximate historical territories. They are deliberately coarse (a few vertices) and are always intersected with the Natural Earth coastline. They do NOT represent surveyed historical boundaries. Coordinates are [longitude, latitude].

zones.label: Welsh lands west of the Offa's Dyke frontier zone
zones.basis: Follows the general line of Offa's Dyke, used by historians as an indicator of the Anglo-Welsh frontier zone around AD 1000 (Hill 1981; Davies 1991). The real frontier was a zone, not a line, and moved repeatedly.

zones.label: Lower Gwent
zones.basis: Area of early Norman control from Chepstow (begun 1067) westward towards Caerleon (Davies 1991).

zones.label: South Wales lowlands and Brycheiniog (Anglo-Norman March)
zones.basis: Gwent, Glamorgan, Gower, Kidwelly, Brycheiniog and southern Pembrokeshire, conquered from c.1081–1093 and largely held by marcher lords thereafter (Davies 1991; Rees 1959). Welsh rulers recovered parts of this zone at times.

zones.label: Perfeddwlad (between the Conwy and the Dee)
zones.basis: The 'Four Cantrefs' ceded to the English Crown by the Treaty of Aberconwy (1277).

zones.label: Gwynedd west of the Conwy (Gwynedd Uwch Conwy) with Anglesey and Meirionnydd
zones.basis: Territory left to Llywelyn ap Gruffudd by the Treaty of Aberconwy (1277).

zones.label: Lothian (between the Forth and the Tweed)
zones.basis: Region between the Firth of Forth and the Tweed, part of the earldom of Bamburgh/Northumbria before c.1018 and Scottish thereafter (Woolf 2007).

zones.label: Strathclyde / Cumbria (Clyde valley and south-west)
zones.basis: Core of the British kingdom of Strathclyde (Woolf 2007). Galloway, included here for simplicity, had its own Norse-Gaelic lords.

zones.label: Northern Cumbria (Carlisle district)
zones.basis: District around Carlisle held by the Cumbrian/Scottish kings until William II's seizure in 1092 (ASC; Kapelle 1979).

zones.label: Cumberland, Westmorland and Northumberland (Scottish-held 1136–57)
zones.basis: Areas held by David I and his son Henry after 1136 and under the Treaty of Durham (1139), returned to Henry II in 1157 (Duncan 1975). Bamburgh and Newcastle were formally excluded in 1139.

zones.label: Caithness
zones.basis: Caithness, held by the Norse earls of Orkney under dual overlordship (McNeill and MacQueen 1996). Boundary simplified.

zones.label: Hebrides (Outer and Inner)
zones.basis: Islands of the Kingdom of the Isles ceded by Norway in 1266 (Treaty of Perth). Clip outline simplified around the islands; small mainland slivers may be included.
